title: Growth Hypotheses Notebook & Manager Snippets
content:
Purpose: quick-running, experimental notebook for the next quarter. Use this to (a) capture testable growth hypotheses, (b) track small experiments and outcomes, and (c) prepare micro-snippets for manager syncs and asks. This is intentionally rough — short notes, evidence bullets, and quick scripts I can copy into 1:1s.

Context and constraints:
- Role: Senior People Ops (career ladder stretch to L4 lead-level scope).
- Time horizon: next 12 weeks (rolling).
- Priorities: broaden influence across GTM and Eng, lead one cross-functional initiative end-to-end, improve measurable coaching throughput.

How to use this doc (workflow):
1) Write a single hypothesis in the template below.
2) Design a 2–3 step experiment (1–2 week cadence).
3) Capture signals (metrics + qualitative notes).
4) Add short manager snippet after each experiment.

Hypothesis template (compact):
- Hypothesis: I believe [action] will increase/enable [ability/metric] by [amount] in [timeframe].
- Success metric(s): 1–2 numeric signals + 1 qualitative signal.
- Experiment steps (1–3): quick, verifiable, low friction.
- Risk / counter-evidence to watch for.
- Data sources: Slack threads, survey responses, meeting counts, calendar events, feedback quotes.

----
Hypothesis A — "Lead a GTM cross-team retro to surface friction and ship a low-effort fix"
- Hypothesis: Running a focused GTM x Eng retro + 1 prioritized fix will reduce average time-to-resolution for onboarding blockers by 20% in 8 weeks.
- Success metrics: (1) avg time from blocker report -> resolution (baseline: 7d) -> target 5.5d; (2) # of repeat blocker reports for same category down 30%; (qual) TL feedback: "fewer escalations" in post-retro survey.
- Experiment steps:
  1) Run a 90-minute retro with 8 participants (2x TLs from GTM, 2x Eng PMs, 1x SRE, 1x onboarding ops) — week 1.
  2) Identify top 1 low-effort fix (owner + <2 week implementation plan).
  3) Track the blocker flow for 6 weeks after ship and compare to baseline.
- Risk: retro could surface process issues outside my influence; low engagement from GTM. Mitigation: pre-work + explicit agenda + exec sponsor invite.
- Data sources: support ticket tags, #onboarding Slack thread, post-retro pulse (3 Qs).
- Quick manager snippet after 1 week: "Ran GTM x Eng retro, landed one quick fix owner (Anika) — measuring blockers for 6 weeks; looking for additional support to prioritize Ops time if metrics don't improve."

----
Hypothesis B — "Increase coaching throughput by running a 6-week coaching micro-sprint"
- Hypothesis: A structured 6-week coaching sprint (6 participants, weekly 30-min skill labs + short practice sessions) will improve Mentee self-reported confidence in stakeholder communications by +25 points on a 100-point scale.
- Success metrics: (1) pre/post self-confidence survey (target +25); (2) 2 observed behavioral changes captured in follow-up 1:1s (qual).
- Experiment steps:
  1) Recruit 6 volunteer ICs (mix of GTM/Eng) — week 0.
  2) Run 6 weekly micro-sessions (30 min + 15 min practice homework) focusing on stakeholder framing + escalation etiquette.
  3) Collect pre/post pulse and 1:1 notes.
- Risk: dropoff after week 2. Mitigation: short sessions, homework under 15 min, recognize participants publicly at end.
- Data sources: Google form (pre/post), manager confirmations, 1:1 notes.
- Quick manager snippet after kickoff: "Launching a coaching micro-sprint with 6 volunteers to test repeatable framework; initial recruitment full — will report pre/post signals in 6 weeks. Ask: help amplify with TLs if we need more cohort diversity."

----
Hypothesis C — "Build a tiny playbook for rapid onboarding escalations"
- Hypothesis: Publishing a 1-pager escalation playbook + one live walkthrough will reduce time to first responder by 50% for critical onboarding incidents in 30 days.
- Success metrics: time to first response (baseline: 12h) -> target 6h; adoption: at least 3 teams bookmark + confirm in their runbooks.
- Experiment steps: create 1-pager -> share with 3 pilot teams -> run walkthrough + collect feedback -> iterate.
- Risk: low adoption if not integrated into team runbooks — mitigation: target runbook owners directly, ask TLs to acknowledge.
- Quick manager snippet: "Drafted escalation playbook + pilot scheduled with Sales Ops and Eng onboarding next Tues; will measure response time for 30 days post-walkthrough."

----
Evidence capture format (brief):
- Date | experiment | metric delta | 1 line context | quick quote (if any)
Examples:
- 2026-01-12 | coaching sprint week1 | N/A (baseline) | good attendance, homework completion 5/6 | "that framing made my convo shorter"
- 2026-01-28 | GTM retro fix shipped | time-to-resolution -1.2d | fix rolled by Anika | "already seeing fewer pings"

Manager-prep snippets (copyable) — 15s / 60s / 3min
- 15s elevator (what I want them to remember): "Running three small experiments to measurably improve onboarding and coaching; early traction — will surface metric signals in 6 weeks."
- 60s context + ask: "Trying a GTM x Eng retro to cut onboarding blockers: we landed a small fix and are measuring blocker flow over 6 weeks. If blockers don't drop, I'd like 4 hours/month of dedicated engineer time to test a mid-term fix."
- 3 min quick briefing (for synchronous 1:1):
  1) Why this matters (30s): onboarding blockers cost X hours/month and cause conversion issues; small fixes can change that flow.
  2) What I did (60s): ran a focused retro with key partners, shipped a quick fix owner, instrumenting tickets.
  3) What I need (45s): alignment on priority and an exec sponsor to unblock cross-team resources if metrics don't budge.
  4) Risks & fallback (25s): primary risk is lack of capacity; fallback is to triage only highest-impact categories.

Micro-asks and backup phrasing (for email/slack)
- If you can spare 2 hours: "Can you review the playbook and drop one comment? Want a sanity check on the action checklist. Thanks!"
- If you need to escalate to exec: "Heads up — pilot shows [metric], requesting sponsor time to scale. Happy to sync 15 min with data."

Evidence to collect in 1:1s (my checklist)
- Did you see fewer escalations? (yes/no + example)
- Were fixes actually implemented within the planned timeline?
- Any upstream blockers preventing adoption?
- Quote to save for future narratives (capture verbatim)

Quick log (scratch space)
- 2025-10-15: drafted retro agenda; asked Anika to own the fix.
- 2025-10-22: retro held; TLs signaled curiosity but ask for clear metric.
- 2025-11-02: shipped quick fix; set ticket tag = onboarding-quickfix.
- 2025-11-09: started coaching sprint recruitment (6 volunteers).
- 2026-01-11: mid-cohort pulse — 4/6 report increased confidence.

Unresolved questions / hypothesis pivots
- If adoption stalls, can I move to a bottom-up approach (peer champions in each team) rather than top-down?
- Which metric is most defensible for growth conversations with my manager: time-to-resolution vs percent repeat blockers?
- If coaching sprint improves confidence but not behavior in 1:1s, do I continue or shift focus to manager enablement?

Next steps (two-week cadence)
- Week 1: finish post-retro pulse + measure baseline ticket flow.
- Week 2: publish playbook draft + schedule pilot walkthrough.
- Week 3: run coaching sprint week 1 + collect pre/post signals.
- Week 4: compile early evidence and prep 3min manager briefing.

Sign-off snippet (for reflection at end of quarter):
- "What I learned: small, measurable bets + clear owner reduce inertia. What I'd change: bake measurement into the kickoff so we can act earlier on signals."

Todo (short):
- [ ] Convert post-retro pulse into Google Form (2 questions + optional quote).
- [ ] Add ticket dashboard filter (tag: onboarding-quickfix).
- [ ] Draft single-page escalation playbook and share with pilot teams.
- [ ] Draft manager 3-min slides (1 slide: hypothesis + metric + ask).

Notes to self: keep experiments <6 weeks, focus on ownership not perfection, and always have a single metric to point to in syncs.

End of doc — keep this as my running notebook and copy sensible bits into manager 1:1s and promotion narratives.
